tasks.task: Verify the poetry browsing functionality.
tasks.expected: The user can access a list of poetry, with each entry displaying the title and author clearly.

tasks.task: Test the search function by searching for a specific poem title.
tasks.expected: The search returns results that include the poem with the matching title and no unrelated results.

tasks.task: Test the process of posting new poetry.
tasks.expected: The user can fill out a form to input poetry title, content, and tags, then submit it successfully; the new poem should appear on the website.

tasks.task: Test the functionality for posting a comment on an existing poem.
tasks.expected: The user can submit a comment, and it appears under the poem along with the user's name and timestamp.

tasks.task: Verify that users can navigate to different types of poetry categories.
tasks.expected: Clicking on a category correctly filters and displays poems belonging to that category only.

tasks.task: Verify that the website uses 'light goldenrod' as the background color and 'olive drab' as the component color, as specified in the design requirements.
tasks.expected: The website has a background color of 'light goldenrod' and components (such as buttons, cards, headers, etc.) are styled with the color 'olive drab', accurately reflecting the design instruction.

tasks.task: Open the browse list and click the sparkle button on Salt Meadow four times.
tasks.expected: The sparkle count climbs from 12 to 13, 14, then 15, and the fourth click does not raise it past 15 — the control indicates the 3-sparkle limit is reached.

tasks.task: On Cinders, click the sparkle button twice, then use the take-back control once.
tasks.expected: Cinders' sparkle count reads exactly 13 (12 seeded + 2 given - 1 taken back).

tasks.task: Find Juniper in the browse list.
tasks.expected: A pill badge reading Limerick sits next to Juniper's title, and the poem shows its line count of 5 lines.

tasks.task: Click the sparkle button once on Harbor Glass in the browse list, then open Harbor Glass's own page.
tasks.expected: The poem's page shows 10 sparkles — the same count as the browse card after the click, not the seeded 9.

tasks.task: Type Night Ferry into the search box.
tasks.expected: Night Ferry by Priya Anand appears in the results, and poems that don't match are not shown.

tasks.task: Open the homepage and read the This Week's Board top three on a fresh load.
tasks.expected: The top three read, in order: Harbor Glass (score 17), Wren Song (score 17), Night Ferry (score 15) — Harbor Glass beats Wren Song alphabetically on the tie, and Night Ferry is not first despite having the most sparkles.

tasks.task: Scroll down the board past the top three.
tasks.expected: Cinders and Juniper both show score 14, with Cinders listed above Juniper (alphabetical on the tie).

tasks.task: Open Salt Meadow, post a comment signed Noor reading 'Lovely turn in the last line.', then return to the homepage board.
tasks.expected: Salt Meadow's score reads 14 (12 sparkles + 2 for the new comment) and it now sits below Cinders and Juniper, the other poems at 14, per the alphabetical tie order.

tasks.task: Click the sparkle button on Night Ferry three times, then check the board.
tasks.expected: Night Ferry's score reads 18 and it moves to the #1 spot, above Harbor Glass and Wren Song.

tasks.task: Open the browse list and click the sparkle button on Salt Meadow four times.
tasks.expected: The sparkle count climbs from 12 to 13, 14, then 15, and the fourth click does not raise it past 15 — the control indicates the 3-sparkle limit is reached.

tasks.task: Open the Form Lab and look at the form picker.
tasks.expected: Haiku shows 2 published poems already on the site, Sonnet shows 2, Free Verse shows 2, and Limerick shows 1.

tasks.task: In the Form Lab pick Haiku and type four lines into the checker: 'cold stars', 'a lantern gutters', a blank line, then 'snow begins'.
tasks.expected: The live line counter reads 3 — the blank line is not counted — and the Certify button becomes enabled.

tasks.task: In the Form Lab pick Haiku and type just two lines into the checker: 'cold stars' and 'a lantern gutters'.
tasks.expected: While typing, the line counter reads 2, the word count reads 5, and the Certify button stays disabled — all without pressing any submit.

tasks.task: In the Form Lab pick Limerick, load Juniper into the checker, certify it, then find Juniper in the browse list.
tasks.expected: The checker counts Juniper's 5 lines so the limerick requirement is met and Certify enables; after certifying, Juniper's browse entry shows a form-true mark next to its Limerick pill badge.

tasks.task: Open the homepage and read the This Week's Board top three on a fresh load.
tasks.expected: The top three read, in order: Harbor Glass (score 17), Wren Song (score 17), Night Ferry (score 15) — Harbor Glass beats Wren Song alphabetically on the tie, and Night Ferry is not first despite having the most sparkles.

tasks.task: Open the Contests page on a fresh load.
tasks.expected: The Turning Tide shows two entries with Cinders listed above Salt Meadow, both at 12 sparkles — alphabetical order on the tie, even though Salt Meadow entered first.

tasks.task: Try to enter Wren Song into the contest.
tasks.expected: The entry is refused with a clear message that the contest accepts haiku only, and the entries list still shows only the existing entries.

tasks.task: Click Close Voting on The Turning Tide and confirm.
tasks.expected: A confirmation is asked before voting closes; after confirming, Cinders is crowned winner (taking the 12-12 tie alphabetically) and the winner is shown off on the homepage.

tasks.task: Start a fresh contest entry on the Contests page as poet Lena Brook titled Tideline and type two lines, 'grey tide turning' and 'a gull writes its name'; then add a third line 'on the wet sand' and submit.
tasks.expected: With only two lines the submit stays disabled per the haiku line check; after the third line it enables, and Tideline joins the entries list with 0 sparkles, below the two 12-sparkle entries.

tasks.expected: The live line counter reads 3 — the blank line is not counted — and the Certify button becomes enabled.

tasks.task: On Wren Song's critique form enter the name Ada, pick rhythm as the focus, type 'Nice.' and submit; then replace the note with 'The middle stanza loses momentum but the closing image really lands well.' and submit again.
tasks.expected: The short note is rejected with a clear too-short message and no critique is added; the longer note submits, and Wren Song's critique count reads 2.

tasks.task: Open Juniper's page, switch on its feedback-welcome toggle, then open the Critique Corner.
tasks.expected: Juniper shows a feedback-welcome badge and appears at the top of the corner with 0 critiques, ahead of the poems that already have critiques.

tasks.task: In the Critique Corner, mark The Unsent Letter's request as resolved.
tasks.expected: A confirmation is asked before it is retired; after confirming, The Unsent Letter leaves the corner and its poem page shows a Critiqued stamp.

tasks.task: Open My Anthology on a fresh load, before adding anything.
